claims.text: A client whose request timed out cannot tell whether the server processed it: the request may have been lost, or the server may have completed it and only the response was lost.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9110 §9.2.2 (idempotent methods and automatic retry after a communication failure)

claims.text: Đơn Hàng stage-2: OrdersController.Create binds the optional header with [FromHeader(Name = "Idempotency-Key")] string? idempotencyKey (null when absent) and passes it to OrderService.PlaceOrderAsync. Idempotency-Key is presented as Đơn Hàng's convention.

PlaceOrderAsync: with a key, it looks up an order by key (FindByIdempotencyKeyAsync); found for the same customer -> returns it with Created = false and writes nothing; found for another customer -> ArgumentException, answered 400 by ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.

On a retry OrdersController.Create still returns CreatedAtAction: 201 with the earlier order (same id, status, items); placedAt can differ in its last digit: PostgreSQL timestamptz keeps microseconds, the first body serialises .NET's 100 ns in-memory value.
The key is stored in the order's own row (column orders.idempotency_key, set in the Order initializer), so it is written by the same INSERT as the order.

EF Core applies all changes of one SaveChanges/SaveChangesAsync call in a single database transaction by default when the provider supports transactions; in PlaceOrderAsync that covers the order row, its items and the notification row.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs, Transactions: default transaction behavior of SaveChanges; OrderService.cs:25-33

claims.text: DonHangDbContext declares a unique index on Order.IdempotencyKey (HasIndex(...).IsUnique(), migration IX_orders_idempotency_key); PostgreSQL refuses an INSERT whose key already exists in the table.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: DonHangDbContext.cs:55-59; PostgreSQL 17 docs, Unique Indexes (§11.6)

claims.text: A PostgreSQL unique index (default NULLS DISTINCT) allows any number of rows where the indexed column is NULL, so orders placed without a key (idempotency_key NULL) are not duplicates of each other.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, Unique Indexes / CREATE INDEX NULLS [NOT] DISTINCT

claims.text: Two simultaneous requests with one key can both find no order; the unique index lets one INSERT through; the other SaveChangesAsync fails (DbUpdateException, unique violation), writes nothing, and ExceptionHandlingMiddleware answers 409 Conflict, detail: the same request is already being processed.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.cs:52-60; OrderService.cs:15-33; EF Core docs, SaveChanges exceptions

claims.text: A client that retries after that 409 with the same key gets the order the first request created, because the lookup now finds it (middleware detail: 'retry it to get its result').
PUT and DELETE are idempotent methods by definition in HTTP semantics (sending one several times has the same intended effect as once); POST is not idempotent.

idempotent-order.sh signs in as customer 1, makes one key, sends the same POST twice: both 201, same id; last line: customer 1 gained 1 order. Its "same order id" line always prints yes at stage-2 (line 27 has byte 0x01 instead of \1).
Only the client knows whether a request is a retry of an intended order or a new order; comparing items cannot tell a retry from a genuine repeat order.
claims.source_hint: reasoning from the outline misconception; no official source
